security_privacy_cost_impact: Raises the bar on CI: the application job's test now refuses a custom shell or defaults (a soft or empty run:) and any write to the job's environment or PATH file that the job's text names. No credential, secret, personal data, provider call or dependency change; ci.yml is unchanged.
compatibility_impact: No contract changes; ci.yml as on main passes both new readings.
known_limitations: THE RESIDUAL (stated in the test's comments): the reader sees the application job's text, not what runs or what is evaluated. Not seen: a token assembled at run time by the shell (${!name}, concatenation, eval, decoding) or by the runner from a `${{ }}` expression (e.g. ${{ format('GITHUB_{0}', 'ENV') }}, A1-287-3); a glob reaching the runner's file-command files without naming them; `set +e` or `bash +e`/`sh -c` in a run body; and writes or swallowed failures inside programs a step runs (repository scripts, npm scripts, package code, the pinned actions; actions/setup-node writes $GITHUB_PATH by design). Held by the review of every ci.yml and script change, A1-257-4's step-list pin and A1-AUD1015-1's order. Also not refused: a `run:` body line that writes a file later steps or tools read without naming either token (npm's user or project configuration by `npm config set` or a write to `~/.npmrc`, including `node-options=`, which undoes the job's `NODE_OPTIONS: ''`; a project `.npmrc` created at run time; an executable that shadows a command in a directory already on PATH) reaches the same effects, is read and not refused, and is held by the review of every ci.yml change and A1-257-4's step-list pin (A1-287r2-1).
The bootstrap job is not read for shell: or $GITHUB_ENV; a job's environment file reaches only that job's later steps, and the two findings named the application job.
The token readings fail closed: a future run body that merely mentions the word shell, defaults, GITHUB_ENV or GITHUB_PATH fails the test and needs a governance change.
